clue.text: A quick one in S London 'otel?

parts.note: Lewisham is a district of south London
the apostrophe drops the H, cockney style, so a hotel brand becomes 'ilton

explanation.surface: A cheeky request for a quickie in a south London hotel, said with a dropped aitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'otel tells you to drop the H from Hilton too, leaving ILTON; LEWISHAM + ILTON gives LEWIS HAMILTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Hamilton is a Formula One world champion, so he is a very fast racing driver.

clue.text: Left area Tory in charge, rather Spartan

parts.note: standard abbreviation for left
standard abbreviation for area
short for Conservative, the Tory party
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A political report: a Tory politician leaves an area under a rather austere regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech is terse and economical, like the famously curt Spartans of ancient Laconia.

clue.text: With kart roof damaged, could be an expensive paint job

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of its proper shape, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A go-kart with a dented roof needs a respray that might cost a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: A paint job usually means a car respray; here it is a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A valuable painting is a costly piece of artistic labour with paint, a playful sense of paint job.

clue.text: Lip or cheek?

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like parts of the face, but each is slang for impertinence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is informal British slang for impudence, as are lip and cheek, so all three are interchangeable.

clue.text: Gold, best method for crafting 14?

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
top means best
an art is a skill or method of making something

explanation.surface: Asking which gold-working technique is best for making some object.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 refers to the answer at 14-down, BRAKE DISC.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake disc is one component of a car, so it is an example of a motor component; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Heartless juvenile put in prison

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letters of the word are taken out

parts.note: juvenile behaviour is childish

explanation.surface: A cruel young offender is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the middle two letters AT from IMMATURE leaves IMMURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To immure someone is to enclose or confine them within walls, so lock them away.

clue.text: Poor, dear Lotte suffered

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the following letters are in a bad state needing rearrangement

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Pity poor Lotte, who has been through hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffered in the sense of put up with or endured something, which is what tolerated means.

clue.text: Anxious northern Republican in electric car parked on yard

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: EV stands for electric vehicle
R is the abbreviation for Republican
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A worried northern Republican sits in an electric car parked in a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside EV to make ERV; N goes before it and Y after, since the car is parked on the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervy is British informal for jittery or nervous, so anxious is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Uptight about 16, to do with a terminal

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: anal is informal for fussy and uptight
16-down is OVERDRAFT, abbreviated OD in banking

explanation.surface: Someone tense about their overdraft at the airport terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: OD, the bank-statement abbreviation for overdrawn or overdraft, sits inside ANAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodal means relating to an anode, the positive electrode or terminal of a battery or cell.

clue.text: Critic unhappy about last section of Baku track

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other
unhappy suggests something disturbed and out of sorts, so the letters get jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the final part of a word is just its closing letter here

parts.note: the final letter of Baku

explanation.surface: A reviewer is disappointed by the final part of the Baku Grand Prix street track.
explanation.walkthrough: CIRCIT goes round U to give CIRCUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing circuit is the closed track that cars drive round in a Grand Prix.

clue.text: Pound to get into Carmen, flipping Carmen!

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it
flipping something turns it over and messes up its order, and it doubles as a mild oath

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about money and the opera Carmen.
explanation.walkthrough: The final Carmen is read as car men; MCAREN takes in L to give MCLAREN.
explanation.definitionFit: McLaren is a British Formula One team and sports-car maker, so its people are literally car men.

clue.text: Nobody has energy after twelve o'clock

indicators.note: after tells you which piece follows which in the final order

parts.note: midday
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: No one has any energy left after midday.
explanation.definitionFit: No-one and nobody are both pronouns meaning not a single person.

clue.text: Painted a picture of weak commerce, as some might say

indicators.note: this points to how the words are pronounced by speakers, not how they are spelt

parts.note: poor means weak and trade means commerce

explanation.surface: An economic commentator paints a bleak picture of sluggish business.
explanation.walkthrough: In accents where poor rhymes with pour, poor trade is spoken the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray someone is to depict them, whether in a painting or in words.

clue.text: Watch amber signals covering where I might send you

indicators.note: the words cover the answer, which lies concealed across them

parts.note: the run of letters across the three words

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the traffic lights turning amber.
explanation.walkthrough: The I is the setter, who might send a puzzled solver to look up a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers is the dictionary crossword setters and solvers traditionally consult, so a setter would point you there.

clue.text: Fans backed Sir 1A stopping because of this

indicators.note: to fan something is to spread it out, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Supporters stood behind Sir Lewis Hamilton.
explanation.walkthrough: Fans looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is a verb meaning spreads out. 1A is LEWIS HAMILTON, who was knighted.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing car slows when pads grip the brake disc, so Hamilton stops thanks to this component.

clue.text: Walk in the park, maybe something from Baker Street first

indicators.note: first tells you to place that piece at the front of the answer

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
a bread roll is something a baker makes

explanation.surface: A stroll in Regent's Park after some Sherlock Holmes sightseeing on Baker Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Baker Street splits apart: the baker supplies one piece, the street another. Lance Stroll is also an F1 driver, referred to at 20-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle walk in the park is an example of a leisurely amble, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: In public, doctor initially admitted falsifying bank credit

indicators.note: in places one set of letters inside another

parts.note: overt means open and public
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only opening letters are taken

parts.note: first letter of admitted
first letter of falsifying

explanation.surface: A doctor publicly confessed to fraud over a bank loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In public' reads as 'openly', but it is an instruction: the doctor's pieces go inside the word for public.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft is a facility letting a customer withdraw more than their balance, a form of borrowing from the bank.

clue.text: Takeaway delivery for one's best friend?

definitions.text: Takeaway delivery for one's best friend?

parts.note: surface reading: a takeaway meal delivered to your door
setter's reading: leftovers taken home from a restaurant, supposedly for the dog, man's best friend

explanation.walkthrough: Takeaway suggests food delivery; here it is leftovers you take away from a restaurant meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A container of restaurant leftovers to take home, nominally for a pet dog, man's best friend.

clue.text: Start in Calvi, regularly lost without this!

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Setting off from Calvi in Corsica, the driver keeps getting lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Calvi is a port in Corsica.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite navigation device gives directions, so a driver would get lost without one.

clue.text: You exchange one for old metal

indicators.note: to exchange is to swap one thing for another in its place

parts.note: you, the person doing the crossword
Roman numeral one
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Trading in one coin for some old metal.
explanation.walkthrough: You is the person reading, the SOLVER; swapping its O for an I gives SILVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is a precious metallic chemical element, symbol Ag.

clue.text: Vehicle trial, according to Spooner, giving awful driver break

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: Mr Toad of The Wind in the Willows is a notoriously reckless motorist, and a rest is a break; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A car is test-driven, and the hopeless driver gets a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of TOAD REST gives ROAD TEST. Mr Toad is the car-mad hero of a classic English children's book.
explanation.definitionFit: A road test is a trial of a car's performance on public roads.

clue.text: Ghastly place where 15 retires?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: informal for the worst place imaginable
second meaning: the pit lane, where the racing driver at 15 pulls out of a race

explanation.walkthrough: 15 is Lance STROLL, an F1 driver; retires means drops out of the race rather than goes to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awful is informally called the pits, and in motor racing a car leaving the race goes into the pit lane.

clue.text: Motor racing legend touring Italy's Anglicised city

indicators.note: touring means going all round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: Ayrton Senna, the Brazilian F1 champion
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Ayrton Senna on a tour of an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Siena is a Tuscan city; Sienna is the English spelling, as used for the earth pigment named after it.

clue.text: Table G9 reviewed, paying attention

parts.note: a table of data is a list

indicators.note: re-viewed suggests looking back over it, so it is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: G followed by the number spelt out

explanation.surface: A table numbered G9 has been checked over.
explanation.walkthrough: G9 may look like the G7 summit's bigger sibling, but it is just the letter G and the word nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Listening means attending closely to what is being said, so heeding or paying attention.

clue.text: Rock Hudson finally breaking small part of foot

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: a toe is part of a foot

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: the last letter of Hudson

explanation.surface: Film star Rock Hudson breaks a small bone in his foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock Hudson reads as a person, but Rock is the definition and Hudson only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone is a piece of rock, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Avoid day getting caught up in Musk's old project

indicators.note: being caught up in something means ending up inside it

parts.note: DOGE, the Department of Government Efficiency, was Elon Musk's US government cost-cutting effort
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Steer clear of the day you get dragged into Elon Musk's former venture.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to evade or sidestep it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Philanthropist invested in Lando Norris

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the answer sits within the following words

parts.note: the letters spanning the two names

explanation.surface: A benefactor puts money into F1 driver Lando Norris's career.
explanation.definitionFit: A philanthropist gives money to good causes, as a benefactor or donor does.

clue.text: Smiley for one lacks cold passion

indicators.note: to lack something is to be without it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a smiley face is an example of a typed face symbol
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A smiley face in a text message is no substitute for real warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion is a strong feeling, and an emotion is any strong feeling.

clue.text: British English… the greatest language!

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
ENG is the abbreviation for English
Muhammad Ali called himself the greatest

explanation.surface: A patriot boasts that British English is the finest language in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The greatest looks like praise of English but is the boxer Muhammad Ali's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the language of Bangladesh and West Bengal, spoken by hundreds of millions.

clue.text: Greece has tax reforms, to include new cross-border pricing

indicators.note: reforming something means reshaping it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
